generator: ElevenLabs Sound Effects v2 (eleven_text_to_sound_v2) via the project owner's ElevenLabs account
processing: Each kept take was mixed to mono, high-passed at 700 Hz (500 Hz for blackbird song and wing flutter) and gently low-passed at 11 kHz, both at 12 dB per octave. Leading and trailing silence was trimmed, keeping about 40 ms before the first note. Four takes opened mid-note (robin-tick a, b and c, and blackbird-alarm b), so their start moved to just before the first whole note. Every file has a 10 ms fade-in and a 100 ms fade-out, or 60 ms for the ticks, alarm calls and flutters. Each file was levelled so the RMS of its active part sits at -20 dBFS with sample peaks under -1.5 dBFS. The wing flutters have sharp wingbeats, so a look-ahead limiter took 2.4 and 4.6 dB off their peaks; they sit near -22 and -23 dBFS and keep their pulse depth. Files are mono 44.1 kHz MP3 (LAME VBR -q:a 5, about 52 to 86 kbps) with no tags.
selection: Three takes were generated per sound, 30 in all. The wing flutter was then re-run with a new prompt for three more. Each take was measured for duration, peak, RMS, clipping, share of energy between 1.5 and 10 kHz, longest silent gap, envelope depth and note onsets. Every song and call take was bright (over 99% of its energy in 1.5 to 10 kHz) and made of discrete tonal notes (21 to 63 dB envelope depth, 3 to 12 onsets per second), so none looked like wind or noise. chaffinch-song-a was rejected because it clips: it decodes over full scale, peaking at +1.2 dBFS with 18 samples at or over 0 dBFS. None of the first three flutter takes was a real flutter. wing-flutter-a was a thin whirr at 9 to 11 kHz, wing-flutter-b was pure tones at 3.3 to 4.6 kHz (a chirp), and wing-flutter-c was near-silent. In the retake, wing-flutter-d and wing-flutter-f are soft, feathery noise with clear wingbeat pulses (10 to 12 a second, 21 to 23 dB deep) that survive the 500 Hz high-pass, so they replace the first batch. wing-flutter-e was rejected: most of its energy is hiss above 10 kHz, it has no wingbeat pulses, and it is near-silent after the high-pass (-47 dBFS). That leaves 28 files: three per sound, and two each for chaffinch song and wing flutter.
